When recording the time since the last HIV test, specify the number and the unit (e.g., days, weeks, months, or years). If the test was self-administered by the recipient, indicate this by marking the appropriate field. For other end-users, record their sex (M for male, F for female) and age in years. If the individual has a sexual partner, indicate this as Yes or No, and provide the partner's sex and age if applicable. For HIV self-test details, include the test name, kit lot number (letters and numbers only), expiry date (in the format dd/mm/yy), and serial number. Record the visit date (day, month, year), provider ID, and distribution point code. Distribution point types include various facilities such as voluntary counseling and testing (VCT), antenatal care (ANC), inpatient services, sexually transmitted infection (STI) clinics, prevention of mother-to-child transmission (PMTCT) follow-up, pediatric services, voluntary medical male circumcision (VMMC), malnutrition clinics, tuberculosis (TB) clinics, outpatient departments (OPD), and other community-based or mobile services. When documenting condom distribution, specify the type (male or female), the number distributed, and the age of the recipient. For each record, include the visit date, provider ID, and distribution point code. Indicate the recipient's sex (M/F), whether they are new to antiretroviral therapy (ART), currently on ART, or have an inconclusive status. If the test was self-administered, mark Yes or No accordingly. If an error is made in recording data, correct it by shading the incorrect field and marking the correct response. For example, if Yes was marked in error, shade it and mark No instead. Similarly, if an error occurs in a box, shade the incorrect entry and write the correct answer nearby. To discard an entire page, mark Discard Whole Page without crossing out the entire record or page. Mandatory questions are marked with an asterisk ().
